subproblem.title: Appendix A.4: abstract dimension-reduction theorem
subproblem.statement: Appendix A.4 with the additional hypothesis (H0). Let P, n, Q ∈ ℕ, let F be a set of functions φ : ℝ^P → ℝ^Q, and let sing be any map from functions ℝ^P → ℝ^Q to subsets of ℝ^P. Write φ_{y,λ}(x) := φ(y + λx), μH[n] for the (unnormalized) n-dimensional Hausdorff measure on ℝ^P, and say that a sequence φ_k converges weakly to φ if ∫ f·φ_k dμH[n] → ∫ f·φ dμH[n] for every continuous compactly supported f : ℝ^P → ℝ. Assume: (H0) two members of F that agree μH[n]-a.e. are equal; (H1) every φ ∈ F is locally μH[n]-integrable; (A.1) φ_{y,λ} ∈ F whenever φ ∈ F, 0 < λ < 1 and |y| ≤ 1 − λ; (A.2) for every φ ∈ F, every y with |y| < 1 and every strictly decreasing sequence λ_k > 0 with λ_k → 0, there are a strictly increasing sequence of indices k_i and ψ ∈ F such that φ_{y,λ_{k_i}} converges weakly to ψ and ψ(λx) = ψ(x) for all λ > 0 and all x; (A.3) for every φ ∈ F: sing φ is closed; sing φ = ∅ whenever φ = c·1_L for some c ∈ ℝ^Q and some n-dimensional linear subspace L; sing φ_{y,λ} = {x : y + λx ∈ sing φ} whenever 0 < λ < 1 and |y| ≤ 1 − λ; and whenever φ_k ∈ F converge weakly to φ, for every ε > 0 there is k₀ with B_1(0) ∩ sing φ_k ⊆ {x : dist(x, sing φ) < ε} for all k ≥ k₀ (the right side being empty if sing φ = ∅). Then either (I) B_1(0) ∩ sing φ = ∅ for every φ ∈ F, or (II) there is an integer d with 0 ≤ d ≤ n − 1 such that μH[d + α](sing φ ∩ B_1(0)) = 0 for every φ ∈ F and every real α > 0; there are ψ ∈ F and a d-dimensional linear subspace L with sing ψ = L and ψ(y + λx) = ψ(x) for all y ∈ L, λ > 0 and x; and, if d = 0, sing φ ∩ B_σ(0) is finite for every φ ∈ F and every σ < 1.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Appendix A, A.1–A.5 and the proof of A.4 (chapter-A.txt lines 8–153 = chapter-07-source.txt lines 1099–1255). Departures: [D1] (H0) is added: the book treats members of F modulo H^n-null sets (its identities ψ_{y,1} = ψ are identities of weak limits) while sing acts on functions; (H0) makes this rigorous and holds for the canonical density functions of the applications. [D2] the book's "evidently" for ψ_{βx,1} = ψ needs the uniform bound (c) below. [D3] in the induction the point x must be taken in the H^ℓ-full set of step 5 (so that ψ ∈ F^ℓ). [D4] "3.6(2) of Ch. 1" means Ch. 1, 3.26(2).
0. Facts. (a) If u is locally H^n-integrable and ∫ fu dH^n = 0 for all f ∈ C_c then u = 0 H^n-a.e. (on each ball B with compact closure, |u|H^n⌞B is a finite Borel measure, so u/|u| is an L¹(|u|H^n⌞B)-limit of continuous compactly supported fields); with (H0), two members of F that are weak limits of one sequence coincide. (b) H^n is translation invariant and H^n(μA) = μ^nH^n(A); so g_k ⇀ g implies (g_k)_{y,1} ⇀ g_{y,1}, and ∫f(x)g(μx)dH^n = μ^{−n}∫f(w/μ)g(w)dH^n. (c) If g_k ⇀ g, Banach–Steinhaus on {f ∈ C(ℝ^P) : spt f ⊆ K} (K compact, sup norm) bounds the functionals f ↦ ∫fg_k dH^n uniformly in k; hence μ_k → 1 implies (g_k)_{0,μ_k} ⇀ g, since ‖f(·/μ_k) − f‖_∞ → 0. (d) With h^ℓ_∞(A) := inf{Σ(diam C_j)^ℓ : A ⊆ ∪C_j}: H^ℓ(A) = 0 ⇔ h^ℓ_∞(A) = 0; h^ℓ_∞(y+λA) = λ^ℓh^ℓ_∞(A); for bounded Borel A, limsup_{ρ↓0} ρ^{−ℓ}h^ℓ_∞(A ∩ B_ρ(x)) ≥ c_ℓ > 0 for H^ℓ-a.e. x ∈ A (Ch. 1, 3.26(2)). Say ψ is L-invariant if ψ(y+λx) = ψ(x) for y ∈ L, λ > 0.
1. Lemma T. If φ ∈ F, x ∈ sing φ ∩ B_1(0), λ_k ↓ 0 with λ_k ≤ (1−|x|)/2 and φ_{x,λ_k} ⇀ ψ ∈ F along a subsequence, then 0 ∈ sing ψ: 0 ∈ sing φ_{x,λ_k} by A.3(2), the φ_{x,λ_k} lie in F (A.1), so A.3(3) puts points of sing ψ arbitrarily close to 0, and sing ψ is closed.
2. Lemma S. If ψ ∈ F is L-invariant, A.3(2) gives z ∈ sing ψ ⇔ y+λz ∈ sing ψ for 0<λ<1, |y| ≤ 1−λ, hence (composing) for all y ∈ L, λ > 0; if sing ψ ≠ ∅ then L ⊆ sing ψ (dilate z+L to 0, closedness). Homogeneous ψ have conical sing ψ.
3. A.5. If ψ ∈ F is L-invariant with dim L ≥ n, then ψ = ψ(0)·1_{L'} for an n-dimensional L' ⊆ L and sing ψ = ∅: for x ∉ L', ψ ≡ ψ(x) on the relatively open half {y+λx : y ∈ L', λ>0} of an (n+1)-plane, which has infinite H^n-measure near each of its points, so local integrability forces ψ(x) = 0; ψ(y) = ψ(0) on L'. If dim L > n, ψ(0) = 0 as well.
4. If some sing φ meets B_1(0), let 𝒟 := {dim L : some L-invariant ψ ∈ F has sing ψ ≠ ∅}. Lemma T with A.2 gives a homogeneous ψ with 0 ∈ sing ψ, so 0 ∈ 𝒟; by step 3 elements of 𝒟 are ≤ n−1. Put d := max 𝒟 (so n ≥ 1; if n = 0 the first alternative holds).
5. Book (1). Let ℓ ≥ 0, F^ℓ := {φ ∈ F : H^ℓ(sing φ ∩ B_1(0)) > 0}, φ ∈ F^ℓ, A := sing φ ∩ B_1(0). For H^ℓ-a.e. x ∈ A there are λ_k ↓ 0 and a homogeneous ψ ∈ F^ℓ with φ_{x,λ_k} ⇀ ψ. Proof: by (d) choose λ_k ↓ 0, λ_k ≤ (1−|x|)/2, with h^ℓ_∞(A ∩ B_{λ_k}(x)) ≥ (c_ℓ/2)λ_k^ℓ, and ψ by A.2. If H^ℓ(sing ψ ∩ B_1(0)) = 0 then, sing ψ being a cone, h^ℓ_∞(sing ψ) = 0; cover sing ψ by open balls B_{ρ_j}(x_j) with Σ(2ρ_j)^ℓ < ε. K := B̄_1(0) ∖ ∪B_{ρ_j}(x_j) is compact and disjoint from the closed set sing ψ; by A.3(3), for large k, B_1(0) ∩ sing φ_{x,λ_k} ⊆ ∪B_{ρ_j}(x_j), so h^ℓ_∞(B_1(0) ∩ sing φ_{x,λ_k}) < ε. By A.3(2) this set is λ_k^{−1}(A ∩ B_{λ_k}(x) − x), so h^ℓ_∞(A ∩ B_{λ_k}(x)) < ελ_k^ℓ: a contradiction for ε < c_ℓ/2.
6. Lemma I (book lines 125–134). Let φ ∈ F be S-invariant, x ∈ B_1(0) ∖ S, λ_k ↓ 0, φ_{x,λ_k} ⇀ ψ ∈ F, ψ homogeneous. Then ψ is (S+ℝx)-invariant. Proof: homogeneous ψ has ψ_{w,1} = ψ_{θw,θ} ∈ F for θ = 1/(2+|w|) (A.1). For y ∈ S, (φ_{x,λ_k})_{y,1} = φ_{x,λ_k}, so ψ_{y,1} = ψ by (b), (a). For β ∈ ℝ, homogeneity of φ gives (φ_{x,λ_k})_{βx,1} = (φ_{x,λ_k})_{0,μ_k}, μ_k = (1+βλ_k)^{−1} → 1, so by (b), (c), (a) ψ_{βx,1} = ψ. Combine with homogeneity.
7. Dimension bound (book lines 113–141). For real ℓ > d, F^ℓ = ∅, i.e. H^{d+α}(sing φ ∩ B_1(0)) = 0 for all φ, α > 0. Otherwise step 5 gives a homogeneous φ¹ ∈ F^ℓ; given φ ∈ F^ℓ invariant under a j-dimensional S, j ≤ d < ℓ, H^ℓ(S) = 0 lets us pick x ∉ S in the good set of step 5, and Lemma I gives ψ ∈ F^ℓ invariant under S+ℝx. At j = d+1 this contradicts the maximality of d.
8. Existence of ψ (book lines 134–139). Take φ ∈ F, L-invariant, dim L = d, sing φ ≠ ∅, so L ⊆ sing φ. If z ∈ sing φ ∖ L, x := z/(2|z|) ∈ sing φ ∩ B_1(0) ∖ L; A.2 with λ_k = (1−|x|)/(k+2) gives ψ with 0 ∈ sing ψ (Lemma T) invariant under L+ℝx (Lemma I), contradicting d = max 𝒟. So sing φ = L.
9. d = 0 (book lines 142–153). Suppose sing φ ∩ B_σ(0) is infinite, σ < 1: distinct x_k ∈ sing φ ∩ B_σ(0) converge to some x (∈ sing φ, |x| ≤ σ); pass to subsequences with λ_k := 2|x_k−x| strictly decreasing, (x_k−x)/|x_k−x| → ξ, and φ_{x,λ_k} ⇀ ψ homogeneous (A.2). z_k := (x_k−x)/λ_k ∈ sing φ_{x,λ_k} ∩ B_1(0) (|z_k| = 1/2), so ξ/2 ∈ sing ψ by A.3(3), and the ray ℝ_{>0}ξ ⊆ sing ψ (Lemma S): H^1(sing ψ ∩ B_1(0)) > 0, contradicting step 7 with α = 1.
proof_key_steps: Weak limits are unique in F (H0); Banach–Steinhaus controls moving dilations.
Singular points pass to tangent functions and invariance passes to sing; A.5 gives d ≤ n−1.
Tangent functions at H^ℓ-a.e. singular point keep positive H^ℓ; induction on invariance gives F^ℓ = ∅ for ℓ > d.
Maximality of d gives sing ψ = L; for d = 0 an accumulation point yields a singular ray, a contradiction.

audit.reason: The one-line proposition independently elaborates and matches all stated hypotheses, including H0 and decreasing scales. H0 justifies pointwise identification of weak limits; uniform boundedness handles moving dilations. The tangent-content argument, invariance induction and maximality establish the dimension bound and extremal member, while accumulation produces the contradiction needed for d = 0 finiteness.

subproblem.title: Theorem 7.2.4: compactness of minimizing currents
subproblem.statement: Let U ⊆ ℝ^{n+k} be open and T_j ∈ 𝒟_n(U) minimizing in U (Simon 7.1.1), with sup_j (M_W(T_j) + M_W(∂T_j)) < ∞ for every open W ⊂⊂ U (∂-mass read as 0 when n = 0), and T_j ⇀ T in 𝒟_n(U). Then T is integer multiplicity and minimizing in U, and μ_{T_j} → μ_T as Radon measures in U: for all integer multiplicity representations of the T_j and of T, ∫ f dμ_{T_j} → ∫ f dμ_T for every continuous f with compact support in U.
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon 7.2.4, Remark 2.5(1) and the proof of 2.4 (chapter-07.txt lines 157–288). For any representation R of an integer multiplicity current S, R.measure = μ_S (Ch. 6, 3.2(3)), so it suffices to prove ∫ f dμ_{T_j} → ∫ f dμ_T.
1. Case n = 0. Each T_j is 0 (the point-removal argument: if a representation of T_j had a point x₀ ∈ U, the current with x₀ deleted is an integer multiplicity competitor with spt of the difference {x₀} ⊂ W ⊂⊂ U and strictly smaller M_W). Hence T = 0, which is integer multiplicity (empty carrier) and trivially minimizing, and all representations of 0 have zero measure. Assume n ≥ 1.
2. T is integer multiplicity (Remark 2.5(1)): by Federer–Fleming (Ch. 6, 3.11) a subsequence of T_j converges weakly to an integer multiplicity current, which equals T.
3. Cut-offs (book lines 176–186). Fix a compact K ⊂ U and 0 < ε < dist(K, ∂U); choose ψ ∈ C^∞(U; [0,1]), ψ = 1 near K, spt ψ ⊆ {dist(·,K) < ε}; W_s := {ψ > s} (0 ≤ s < 1), so K ⊂ W_s ⊂⊂ U.
4. Flat convergence (book (2)): by Ch. 6, 7.2 (T, T_j integer multiplicity with the uniform bounds), T − T_j = ∂R_j + S_j with R_j, S_j integer multiplicity and M_{W_0}(R_j) + M_{W_0}(S_j) → 0.
5. Slicing (book (3)–(5)): by Ch. 6, 4.5(1),(2) applied to R_j and ψ, ∫_0^1 M(⟨R_j, ψ, s⟩) ds ≤ Lip(ψ) M_{W_0}(R_j) → 0; passing to a subsequence and using Fatou, choose α ∈ (0,1) with ∂(R_j⌞W_α) = (∂R_j)⌞W_α + P_j, P_j integer multiplicity, spt P_j ⊆ {ψ = α}, M(P_j) → 0, and (excluding countably many α) μ_{T_j}({ψ = α}) = 0 for all j and μ_T({ψ = α}) = 0.
6. Hence (book (6),(7)) T⌞W_α = T_j⌞W_α + ∂R̃_j + S̃_j, R̃_j := R_j⌞W_α, S̃_j := S_j⌞W_α − P_j, with M(R̃_j) + M(S̃_j) → 0, and M((∂R̃_j)⌞{ψ = α}) ≤ M(P_j).
7. Comparison (book (8)–(12)). Let X be integer multiplicity, ∂X = 0, spt X ⊆ K. Y_j := X + ∂R̃_j is an integer multiplicity cycle with spt Y_j ⊆ {ψ ≥ α}, a compact subset of W_γ for γ < α; so T_j + Y_j is a competitor and minimality gives M_{W_γ}(T_j) ≤ M_{W_γ}(T_j + Y_j). Letting γ ↑ α (W_γ ↓ {ψ ≥ α}) and using μ_{T_j}({ψ=α}) = 0, μ_X({ψ=α}) = 0 (α < 1) and step 6: M_{W_α}(T_j) ≤ M_{W_α}(T_j + Y_j) + M(P_j). By step 6, M_{W_α}(T_j + Y_j) ≤ M_{W_α}(T + X) + M(S̃_j). Thus M_{W_α}(T_j) ≤ M_{W_α}(T + X) + ε_j, ε_j := M(P_j) + M(S̃_j) → 0 (book (11)); with X = 0 (book (12)) M_{W_α}(T_j) ≤ M_{W_α}(T) + ε_j. Lower semicontinuity of mass (SimonGMT WeaklyConvergesOn.massOn_le_liminf) gives M_{W_α}(T) ≤ M_{W_α}(T + X) (book (8)).
8. Minimality in the contract's form. Let W ⊂⊂ U be open and S' integer multiplicity with SameBoundary S' T and K := spt(S' − T) compact ⊆ W. Put X := S' − T (integer multiplicity, Ch. 6, 3.2(1); ∂X = 0) and run steps 3–7 with this K and ε < dist(K, ℝ^{n+k}∖W), so W_α ⊆ W. Since μ_{S'} = μ_T on the open set U ∖ K and M_W(T), M_W(S') < ∞, M_W(S') − M_W(T) = μ_{S'}(W_α) − μ_T(W_α) ≥ 0. With step 2, T is minimizing in U.
9. Radon convergence (book (13),(14)). From step 7 with X = 0, limsup_j μ_{T_j}(K) ≤ limsup_j M_{W_α}(T_j) ≤ M_{W_α}(T) ≤ μ_T({dist(·,K) < ε}); letting ε ↓ 0, limsup_j μ_{T_j}(K) ≤ μ_T(K). This was proved for a subsequence of an arbitrary subsequence, hence holds for the whole sequence. Lower semicontinuity gives μ_T(G) ≤ liminf_j μ_{T_j}(G) for open G ⊆ U. For f ∈ C_c(U), f ≥ 0, write ∫ f dμ = ∫_0^∞ μ({f > t}) dt = ∫_0^∞ μ({f ≥ t}) dt (equal for all but countably many t); {f > t} is open, {f ≥ t} (t > 0) compact, so liminf ≥ and limsup ≤ hold for the integrands, and sup_j μ_{T_j}(spt f) < ∞ allows dominated convergence. Splitting f = f⁺ − f⁻ gives ∫ f dμ_{T_j} → ∫ f dμ_T.
proof_key_steps: n = 0 trivial; the limit is integer multiplicity (Federer–Fleming).
Flat decomposition and slicing at a good level give T − T_j = ∂R̃_j + S̃_j locally with small masses.
Comparison with T_j + X + ∂R̃_j and lower semicontinuity give minimality of T.
limsup μ_{T_j}(K) ≤ μ_T(K) and liminf on open sets give Radon convergence.

audit.reason: The proof establishes integrality, minimality and representation-independent mass convergence. The corrected slicing sign and level-set comparison are consistent; localization proves the contract's competitor inequality, and the subsequence argument supplies convergence for the original sequence.

subproblem.title: Lemma 7.2.1: existence of a mass-minimizing integral filling
subproblem.statement: Let m, ℓ ≥ 0, P = m+2+ℓ, and S ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(ℝ^P) integer multiplicity with spt S compact and ∂S = 0. Then there is an integer multiplicity T ∈ 𝒟_{m+2}(ℝ^P) with spt T compact, ∂T = S, and M(T) ≤ M(R) for every integer multiplicity R ∈ 𝒟_{m+2}(ℝ^P) with spt R compact and ∂R = S.
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon 7.2.1 and its proof (chapter-07.txt lines 86–132), with README erratum 2: the conclusion ∂T = S (shown in the printed proof, "T ∈ 𝓘_S") is part of the statement, and n = m+2 ≥ 2 so that S has dimension ≥ 1. Here M(T) = T.mass = M_{ℝ^P}(T).
1. Let 𝓘_S := {R ∈ 𝒟_{m+2}(ℝ^P) : R integer multiplicity, spt R compact, ∂R = S}. 𝓘_S ≠ ∅: the cone R₀ := 0 ⨯ S = h_#([[(0,1)]] × S), h(t,x) = tx (Ch. 6, 2.30), satisfies ∂R₀ = S − 0 ⨯ ∂S = S (2.31, as ∂S = 0 and dim S ≥ 1), is integer multiplicity (Ch. 6, 3.10, via 3.2(2) and 3.9), and spt R₀ ⊆ {tx : 0 ≤ t ≤ 1, x ∈ spt S} is compact.
2. Every R ∈ 𝓘_S has M(R) < ∞ (locally finite mass and compact support). Let m₀ := inf_{R∈𝓘_S} M(R) and choose R_q ∈ 𝓘_S with M(R_q) → m₀ (book (1)).
3. Retraction (book (2),(3)). Fix ρ₀ > 0 with spt S ⊆ B_{ρ₀}(0) and let f be the nearest point retraction of ℝ^P onto the closed ball B̄_{ρ₀}(0); Lip f = 1 and f = id on B̄_{ρ₀}(0). The push-forward f_#R_q (Ch. 6, 2.29 and 3.9; f|spt R_q is proper since spt R_q is compact) is integer multiplicity, spt f_#R_q ⊆ f(spt R_q) ⊆ B̄_{ρ₀}(0), and M(f_#R_q) ≤ (Lip f)^{m+2} M(R_q) = M(R_q). Moreover ∂f_#R_q = f_#∂R_q = f_#S (Ch. 6, 2.24(1) and its Lipschitz extension 2.29), and f_#S = id_#S = S by Ch. 6, 2.28/2.29, because f = id on spt S. Hence f_#R_q ∈ 𝓘_S and M(f_#R_q) → m₀. (Equivalently one may use the smooth 1-Lipschitz map x ↦ g(|x|)x/|x| with g(r) = r on [0, ρ₀], 0 ≤ g' ≤ 1, g ≤ ρ₀+1, which avoids Lipschitz push-forwards.)
4. Compactness (book: Compactness Theorem 3.11 of Ch. 6). sup_q (M(f_#R_q) + M(∂f_#R_q)) ≤ sup_q M(R_q) + M(S) < ∞, so by the Federer–Fleming compactness theorem (Ch. 6, 3.11) a subsequence f_#R_{q'} converges weakly in ℝ^P to an integer multiplicity T ∈ 𝒟_{m+2}(ℝ^P).
5. T ∈ 𝓘_S (book lines 131–132): spt T ⊆ B̄_{ρ₀}(0) (every test form supported in the open complement annihilates all f_#R_{q'}), so spt T is compact; ∂T(ω) = T(dω) = lim f_#R_{q'}(dω) = lim S(ω), i.e. ∂T = S.
6. Minimality (book (4)): by lower semicontinuity of mass under weak convergence (Ch. 6, 2.14; SimonGMT WeaklyConvergesOn.massOn_le_liminf with W = ℝ^P), M(T) ≤ liminf M(f_#R_{q'}) = m₀ ≤ M(R) for every R ∈ 𝓘_S. Every R in the statement belongs to 𝓘_S, which proves the lemma.

Retract into a ball (1-Lipschitz, identity near spt S); Federer–Fleming gives an integer multiplicity limit T ∈ 𝓘_S.
Lower semicontinuity of mass gives M(T) ≤ M(R).

subproblem.title: Lemma 7.1.2: minimizing currents have stationary varifolds with bounded mean curvature
subproblem.statement: Let ℓ ≤ k, U ⊆ ℝ^{n+k} open, N an embedded C² (n+ℓ)-dimensional submanifold with (closure N ∖ N) ∩ U = ∅, and T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) with spt T ⊆ N, T minimizing in N ∩ U (Simon 7.1.1, integer multiplicity competitors) and ∂T = 0 in U (vacuous for n = 0). Then for every integer multiplicity representation R = (M, θ, ξ) of T, the varifold v(M, θ) is stationary in N ∩ U (∫_M θ div_M X dH^n = 0 for all X ∈ C¹_c(U; ℝ^{n+k}) with X(x) ∈ T_xN for x ∈ N ∩ U) and has a generalized mean curvature H in U that is μ_V-essentially bounded on every compact subset of U.
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon 7.1.2 and its proof (chapter-07.txt lines 29–60), with the README erratum 1: the hypotheses spt T ⊆ N and (N̄∖N) ∩ U = ∅ are used, and 1.2(‡) is used in the form "φ = id outside a compact K ⊂ W, φ(N ∩ U) ⊆ N ∩ U" (as printed, K ⊂ W ∩ N makes (‡) vacuous when ℓ < k). Throughout, μ_T = R.measure = θH^n⌞M for every representation (Ch. 6, 3.2(3)), and M_W(T) = μ_T(W) for open W.
1. Case n = 0. Let R represent T and suppose x₀ ∈ M (H^0 is counting measure, so the a.e. conditions on R hold at every point of M; M is locally finite since ∫_{M∩K}θ dH^0 < ∞). Testing T with a 0-form supported near x₀ shows x₀ ∈ spt T ⊆ N. Let S be represented by (M∖{x₀}, θ, ξ); S is integer multiplicity, SameBoundary holds trivially (n = 0), spt(S−T) = {x₀} ⊆ N ∩ U ∩ W for a small open ball W ⊂⊂ U, and M_W(S) = M_W(T) − θ(x₀) < M_W(T), contradicting minimality. So M = ∅, the first variation vanishes identically, and H := 0 works. Assume n ≥ 1 from now on.
2. Support facts. μ_T(U ∖ spt T) = 0, hence H^n(M ∖ N) = 0. Since N is a C¹ submanifold, for H^n-a.e. x ∈ M the approximate tangent space T_xM exists, is the plane oriented by ξ(x) (definition of IMRep) and is contained in T_xN (approximate tangent spaces of subsets of a C¹ submanifold, Ch. 3 §1 and Ch. 2 §4); also div_M X(x) = trace(p_{T_xM}∘DX(x)) = tangentialDivergence (Ch. 4, 2.3).
3. Deformations (book: "φ = φ_t of 2.1 of Ch. 4 with U ∩ N in place of U"; Ch. 4, 2.5–2.6). Let X ∈ C¹_c(U; ℝ^{n+k}) be tangent to N on N ∩ U, K := spt X. X is globally Lipschitz, so it has a C¹ flow φ_t (t ∈ ℝ), each φ_t a C¹ diffeomorphism of U onto U with φ_t = id outside K. N ∩ U is relatively closed in U (because (N̄∖N) ∩ U = ∅) and X|_{N∩U} is a C¹ tangent field on the C² manifold N; integral curves of this tangent field are integral curves of X, so by uniqueness the orbit of a point of N ∩ U stays in N ∩ U (it cannot leave the relatively closed set N ∩ U while staying in K ∪ {x} ⊂ U). Hence φ_t(N ∩ U) ⊆ N ∩ U.
4. Competitors (book (2),(3)). Let S_t := φ_{t#}T, defined from the representation (Ch. 6, 2.24(2), 3.3–3.9): S_t = τ(φ_t(M), θ∘φ_t^{−1}, induced orientation), an integer multiplicity current in U. ∂S_t = 0: choose smooth diffeomorphisms φ^ε of U, equal to the identity outside a fixed compact set, with φ^ε → φ_t in C¹; then φ^ε_#T(dω) = T((φ^ε)^#dω) = T(d(φ^ε)^#ω) = 0 and φ^ε_#T(dω) → S_t(dω) by dominated convergence in the integral formula of 2.24(2). Since φ_t = id off K, spt T ⊆ N and φ_t(N ∩ U) ⊆ N ∩ U, spt(S_t − T) ⊆ K ∩ N is compact. For any open W with K ⊂ W ⊂⊂ U, minimality gives M_W(T) ≤ M_W(S_t) for all t.
5. First variation (book (1)). By the area formula (Ch. 6, 3.2(3), 3.3–3.5; Ch. 4, 1.7–1.8), M_W(S_t) = ∫_{M∩W} J^M φ_t θ dH^n. Since φ_t(x) = x + tX(x) + o(t) in C¹ uniformly on K, d/dt J^Mφ_t(x)|_{t=0} = div_M X(x) with uniform bounds on K, and θ is integrable on K; so t ↦ M_W(S_t) is differentiable at 0 with derivative ∫_M θ div_M X dH^n (Ch. 4, 2.2). The minimum at t = 0 forces this derivative to vanish: R.firstVariation X = 0. This is IsStationaryAlong N.
6. Mean curvature (Ch. 4, 2.7 and 3.14). Let X ∈ C¹_c(U; ℝ^{n+k}) be arbitrary. Choose an open V ⊂ U containing N ∩ spt X on which the nearest point projection π onto N is C¹ (N is C²), let P(z) be the orthogonal projection onto T_zN (C¹ in z ∈ N), χ ∈ C¹_c(V) with χ = 1 near N ∩ spt X, and X^T := χ·P(π(·))X. Then X^T ∈ C¹_c(U) is tangent to N on N ∩ U, so δV(X^T) = 0 by step 5. On N, X − X^T = X^⊥ is normal to N, and at H^n-a.e. x ∈ M (where T_xM ⊆ T_xN by step 2) div_M X^⊥ = −X·H_N(x), H_N(x) := Σ_{i=1}^n B_x(τ_i, τ_i) with τ_i an orthonormal basis of T_xM and B the second fundamental form of N (Ch. 2, 5.9; Ch. 4, 2.7). Hence δV(X) = −∫ X·H dμ_V with H := H_N on M ∩ N and 0 elsewhere (Borel). On a compact K ⊂ U, K ∩ N is compact (N ∩ U relatively closed), B is continuous, so |H| ≤ √n·sup_{K∩N}|B| μ_V-a.e. on K. This is HasLocallyBoundedMeanCurvature. (If ℓ = k, B = 0 and H = 0.)
proof_key_steps: n = 0 gives T = 0; otherwise H^n(M∖N) = 0 and flows of fields tangent to N preserve N ∩ U.
φ_{t#}T are integer multiplicity competitors, so the first variation of their mass vanishes: stationarity in N ∩ U.
Splitting X into tangential and normal parts gives δV(X) = −∫X·H_N dμ_V with H_N locally bounded.

subproblem.title: Theorem 7.3.1: existence and upper semicontinuity of densities; existence of minimizing tangent cones
subproblem.statement: Let ℓ ≤ k, U ⊆ ℝ^{n+k} open, N an embedded C² (n+ℓ)-submanifold with (N̄∖N) ∩ U = ∅, and T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) minimizing in U ∩ N with spt T ⊆ U ∩ N. Then (1) there is Θ: ℝ^{n+k} → ℝ such that Θ^n(μ_T, x) = Θ(x) (limit of M_{B_ρ(x)}(T)/(ω_nρ^n) as ρ ↓ 0, with Θ(x) ≥ 0) for every x ∈ U ∖ spt ∂T, and Θ is upper semicontinuous on U ∖ spt ∂T; (2) for every x ∈ spt T ∖ spt ∂T and every sequence λ_j > 0, λ_j → 0, there are a subsequence λ_{j'} and an integer multiplicity C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^{n+k}), minimizing in ℝ^{n+k}, with η_{x,λ_{j'}#}T ⇀ C in ℝ^{n+k}, μ_{η_{x,λ_{j'}#}T} → μ_C (for all representations), η_{0,λ#}C = C for all λ > 0, and Θ^n(μ_C, 0) = Θ^n(μ_T, x).
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon 7.3.1 and its proof (chapter-07.txt lines 302–364, footnote 2), Remark 2.5(2) (lines 166–174, proof "left to the reader", supplied in step 4), README erratum 3 ((1) on U ∖ spt ∂T, (2) for x ∈ spt T ∖ spt ∂T). For integer multiplicity S, every representation has measure μ_S (Ch. 6, 3.2(3)) and M_W(S) = μ_S(W) for open W.
1. Case n = 0: T is minimizing in U ∩ N with spt T ⊆ N, so deleting any point of a representation would give a competitor of smaller mass; hence T = 0, Θ :≡ 0 works and (2) is vacuous. Assume n ≥ 1.
2. Localization. U' := U ∖ spt ∂T is open and T' := T restricted to U' satisfies ∂T' = 0, spt T' ⊆ N, (N̄∖N) ∩ U' = ∅, and T' is minimizing in U' ∩ N: a competitor S' for T' in W ⊂⊂ U' differs from T' by a compactly supported current, so S := T + (S' − T') (extension by zero) is an integer multiplicity competitor for T with the same boundary and the same masses difference on W.
3. Part (1) (book lines 326–328). By the sibling minimizing_implies_stationary applied to T' in U', V = v(M, θ) is stationary in N ∩ U', hence (Ch. 4, 2.7) has generalized mean curvature H with |H| ≤ Λ_K := √n·sup_{N∩K}|B_N| on each compact K ⊂ U'. By the monotonicity formula with bounded mean curvature (Ch. 4, 3.17; the book cites 4.7–4.9), for ξ ∈ U' and B_{R}(ξ) ⊂ K: F(ρ)ρ^{−n}μ_T(B_ρ(ξ)) is nondecreasing on (0, R) with F(ρ) ∈ [e^{−Λρ}, e^{Λρ}]. Hence Θ(ξ) := lim_{ρ↓0} μ_T(B_ρ(ξ))/(ω_nρ^n) exists in [0, ∞) for every ξ ∈ U', is upper semicontinuous on U' (Ch. 4, 3.11 argument), and Θ ≥ 1 on spt T ∩ U' (θ ≥ 1 a.e. and Ch. 4, 4.10(1)). Set Θ := 0 off U'. Since M_{B_ρ(ξ)}(T) = μ_T(B_ρ(ξ)) for B_ρ(ξ) ⊂ U, HasMassDensity T ξ (Θ ξ) holds on U' = U ∖ boundarySupport T.
4. Lemma BC (blow-up compactness; Remark 2.5(2) for N_j = η_{x_j,λ_j}(N), "left to the reader", proof supplied). Let x ∈ U', x_j → x, λ_j → 0⁺, S_j := η_{x_j,λ_j#}T. A subsequence satisfies S_j ⇀ C in ℝ^{n+k}, C integer multiplicity, ∂C = 0, C minimizing in ℝ^{n+k}, μ_{S_j} → μ_C. Proof: (i) step 3 gives μ_T(B_ρ(z)) ≤ cρ^n near x, so M_{B_R(0)}(S_j) ≤ cR^n and ∂S_j = 0 on B_{r/λ_j}(0) for large j; (ii) Ch. 6, 2.15 (diagonal in R) and 3.11 give a weak limit C (every test form is eventually supported in η_{x_j,λ_j}(U), where currentEval equals S_j) with ∂C = 0, integer multiplicity; (iii) if dist(x_j,N)/λ_j is unbounded, then along a subsequence it tends to ∞, every ball B_R(0) eventually misses η_{x_j,λ_j}(N) ⊇ spt S_j, so C = 0 and μ_{S_j} → 0; otherwise dist(x_j, N) ≤ C₀λ_j for all j and some C₀ < ∞, x ∈ N and, with π the nearest point projection onto N (C¹ near x, π = id on N, Lip(π|B_s(z)) ≤ 1 + cs), the retractions π_j := η_{x_j,λ_j}∘π∘η_{x_j,λ_j}^{−1} onto η_{x_j,λ_j}(N) have Lipschitz constants L_j → 1 on each ball; (iv) run the proof of 2.4: for compact K, a cut-off ψ and W_s := {ψ > s}, Ch. 6, 7.2 gives C − S_j = ∂R_j + S'_j with masses in W_0 → 0, slicing (Ch. 6, 4.5) at a good α gives C⌞W_α = S_j⌞W_α + ∂R̃_j + S̃_j with M(R̃_j) + M(S̃_j) → 0 and boundary error P_j on {ψ = α}, M(P_j) → 0; fix G > 0 with spt ψ ∪ π_j(spt ψ) ⊆ B_G(0) for all large j (|π_j(z) − z| = dist(z, η_{x_j,λ_j}(N)) ≤ |z| + C₀, C₀ as in (iii)); for an integer multiplicity cycle X with spt X ⊆ K put Y_j := X + ∂R̃_j and Z_j := S_j + π_{j#}Y_j (π_{j#} is applied only to the compactly supported Y_j; Ch. 6, 2.24(2), 3.9): ∂Z_j = ∂S_j (as ∂π_{j#}Y_j = π_{j#}∂Y_j = 0) and spt(Z_j − S_j) ⊆ π_j(spt Y_j) ⊆ η_{x_j,λ_j}(N) ∩ B_G(0), so Z_j is a competitor for S_j in η_{x_j,λ_j}(U ∩ N) (dilations preserve minimality); since π_j is C¹ and equals the identity on spt S_j, the push-forward formula (Ch. 6, 2.24(2), 3.3–3.9) gives π_{j#}(S_j⌞B_G(0)) = S_j⌞B_G(0), so Z_j⌞B_G(0) = π_{j#}((S_j + Y_j)⌞B_G(0)) and μ_{S_j}(B_G) ≤ μ_{Z_j}(B_G) ≤ L_j^nμ_{S_j+Y_j}(B_G); comparing off {ψ ≥ α} as in 2.4 (book (9)–(11)), M_{W_α}(S_j) ≤ M_{W_α}(C+X) + M(S̃_j) + M(P_j) + (L_j^n − 1)Λ_G with Λ_G := sup_j μ_{S_j+Y_j}(B_G(0)) ≤ cG^n + M(X) + sup_j M(∂R̃_j) < ∞ (∂R̃_j = (C − S_j)⌞W_α − S̃_j); (v) lower semicontinuity gives M_{W_α}(C) ≤ M_{W_α}(C+X), hence C is minimizing in ℝ^{n+k} (localize to an arbitrary W ⊂⊂ ℝ^{n+k} as in 2.4), and with X = 0, limsup μ_{S_j}(K) ≤ μ_C(K); with lower semicontinuity on open sets and the layer-cake formula, μ_{S_j} → μ_C (for every sub-subsequence, hence for the subsequence). [This replaces footnote 2: competitors are arbitrary in ℝ^{n+k}, so no projection onto T_xN is needed.]
5. Part (2) (book (1)–(4)). Let x ∈ spt T ∖ spt ∂T and apply Lemma BC with x_j = x: S_{j'} ⇀ C, C minimizing, μ_{S_{j'}} → μ_C. For each ρ > 0, (ω_nρ^n)^{−1}μ_{S_j}(B_ρ(0)) = (ω_n(λ_jρ)^n)^{−1}μ_T(B_{λ_jρ}(x)) → Θ(x) (book (1)). Hence HasMassDensity C 0 Θ(x) and HasMassDensity T x Θ(x).
6. Cone property (book lines 342–360). By the sibling minimizing_implies_stationary (ℓ = k, U = N = ℝ^{n+k}), V_C is stationary in ℝ^{n+k}. Since ρ^{−n}μ_C(B_ρ(0)) is constant, the monotonicity identity (Ch. 4, 3.6) gives D^⊥r = 0 μ_C-a.e., i.e. x ∈ T_xV_C, so x ∧ C⃗(x) = 0 μ_C-a.e.; Lemma 2.33 of Ch. 6 (homotopy formula, ∂C = 0, locally finite mass) gives η_{0,λ#}C = C for all λ > 0. As dilation 0 λ '' ℝ^{n+k} = ℝ^{n+k}, currentEval(blowUp C 0 λ, ω) = C(η_{0,λ}^#ω) = C(ω): IsConeCurrent C.

subproblem.title: Theorem 7.4.3 (fixed N): density-one points are regular, stably under weak convergence
subproblem.statement: Let ℓ ≤ k, U ⊆ ℝ^{n+k} open, N an embedded C² (n+ℓ)-submanifold with (N̄∖N) ∩ U = ∅. Let T_i, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) be minimizing in U ∩ N with spt T_i, spt T ⊆ N and ∂T_i = ∂T = 0 in U, sup_i M_W(T_i) < ∞ for every open W ⊂⊂ U, and T_i ⇀ T. If y ∈ N ∩ U has Θ^n(μ_T, y) = 1, y_i ∈ spt T_i and y_i → y, then y ∈ reg T and y_i ∈ reg T_i for all sufficiently large i (reg as in 7.4.1: some ball B_ρ(z) ⊆ U, m ∈ ℤ∖{0} and an embedded oriented C¹ n-submanifold M ∋ z of locally finite H^n-measure in B_ρ(z) with T = m[[M]] in B_ρ(z)).
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon 7.4.3 and its proof (chapter-07.txt lines 617–631), README erratum 5 (N_i = N; the mass bound, which the proof uses through 2.4, is a hypothesis). Allard's theorem is Ch. 5, 5.2 (chapter-05.txt lines 1008–1033), applied with p = 2n.
1. Case n = 0: a minimizing 0-current with support in N vanishes (deleting a point of a representation lowers mass), so μ_T = 0 and Θ(μ_T, y) = 0 ≠ 1; the statement is vacuous. Assume n ≥ 1.
2. Uniform mean curvature. By the sibling minimizing_implies_stationary, the varifolds V_i, V of T_i, T are stationary in N ∩ U; by Ch. 4, 2.7 they have generalized mean curvature H = H_N with |H| ≤ κ := √n·sup_{N ∩ B̄_{2r₀}(y)}|B_N| on B_{2r₀}(y), where B̄_{3r₀}(y) ⊂ U; κ does not depend on i. Monotonicity (Ch. 4, 3.17): for z ∈ B_{r₀}(y), 0 < σ < ρ < r₀, e^{−κσ}σ^{−n}μ(B_σ(z)) ≤ e^{κρ}ρ^{−n}μ(B_ρ(z)) for μ = μ_{T_i}, μ_T; densities exist, and Θ(μ_{T_i}, z) ≥ 1 for z ∈ spt T_i (θ ≥ 1, Ch. 4, 4.10(1)).
3. Lemma M (upper mass bound in the limit; the part of 2.4/2.5(2) used by the book). There are c, c₁ (depending on N near y and on sup_i M_{B_{2r₀}(y)}(T_i)) such that for 0 < ε < ρ < min(r₀/4, 1/(6c)): limsup_i μ_{T_i}(B̄_ρ(y)) ≤ (1+3cρ)^n μ_T(B_{ρ+ε}(y)) + c₁ρ^{n+1}. Proof: let π be the nearest point projection onto N, C¹ on B_{2r₀}(y) with π = id on N, π(y) = y, Lip(π|B_s(y)) ≤ 1 + cs. Take ψ ∈ C^∞, ψ = 1 near B̄_ρ(y), spt ψ ⊂ B_{ρ+ε}(y), W_s := {ψ > s}. By Ch. 6, 7.2 (T_i, T integer multiplicity cycles with uniform mass bounds near y), T − T_i = ∂R_i + S_i with M_{W_0}(R_i) + M_{W_0}(S_i) → 0; slicing (Ch. 6, 4.5) at a good α ∈ (0,1) (along a subsequence; the argument applies to a subsequence of any subsequence) gives T⌞W_α = T_i⌞W_α + ∂R̃_i + S̃_i with M(R̃_i) + M(S̃_i) → 0, boundary error P_i on {ψ = α} with M(P_i) → 0, and μ_{T_i}({ψ=α}) = μ_T({ψ=α}) = 0. Put Z_i := T_i + π_#∂R̃_i (π_# is applied only to the compactly supported integer multiplicity cycle ∂R̃_i; Ch. 6, 2.24(2), 3.9). Since ρ < 1/(6c), Lip(π|B_{3ρ}(y)) ≤ 1 + 3cρ < 3/2 and π(y) = y, so π({ψ ≥ α}) ⊆ π(B_{2ρ}(y)) ⊆ B_{3ρ}(y); hence Z_i is integer multiplicity, ∂Z_i = 0 and spt(Z_i − T_i) ⊆ π(spt ∂R̃_i) is a compact subset of N ∩ G, G := B_{3ρ}(y): Z_i is a competitor for T_i in U ∩ N with W = G. Since π is C¹ and equals the identity on spt T_i ⊆ N, the push-forward formula (Ch. 6, 2.24(2), 3.3–3.9) gives π_#(T_i⌞G) = T_i⌞G, hence Z_i⌞G = π_#((T_i + ∂R̃_i)⌞G); minimality and Lip(π|G) ≤ 1 + 3cρ give μ_{T_i}(G) ≤ μ_{Z_i}(G) ≤ (1+3cρ)^n μ_{T_i+∂R̃_i}(G). As T_i + ∂R̃_i = T_i off {ψ ≥ α}, this yields μ_{T_i}({ψ≥α}) ≤ (1+3cρ)^n μ_{T_i+∂R̃_i}({ψ≥α}) + ((1+3cρ)^n − 1)μ_{T_i}(G), and as in 2.4 (book (9)–(11)) μ_{T_i+∂R̃_i}({ψ≥α}) ≤ μ_T(W_α) + M(S̃_i) + M(P_i). By step 2, μ_{T_i}(G) ≤ c₂ρ^n uniformly in i, which gives the claim.
4. Density ratios (book lines 624–629). Let δ₀ = δ₀(n, k, 2n) be Allard's constant, decreased if necessary so that δ₀ ≤ 1/2 and C(n,k,2n)δ₀^{1/(2n+2)} ≤ 1/4 (C as in Ch. 5, 5.2), and fix η ∈ (0, 1) with (1+2η)^n ≤ 1 + δ₀/4. Since Θ(μ_T, y) = 1, choose ρ ∈ (0, min(r₀/8, 1/(12c))) so small that (1 + 3c(1+η)ρ)^n(1+2η)^n μ_T(B_{(1+2η)ρ}(y))/(ω_n((1+2η)ρ)^n) + 2^{n+1}c₁ρ/ω_n ≤ 1 + δ₀/2, κρ(2ω_n)^{1/(2n)} ≤ δ₀ and e^{κρ}(1 + δ₀) < 2 (possible: as ρ ↓ 0 the first left side tends to (1+2η)^n ≤ 1 + δ₀/4). For large i, |y_i − y| < ηρ, so the closed ball B̄_ρ(y_i) ⊆ B̄_{(1+η)ρ}(y), and Lemma M with radius (1+η)ρ and ε = ηρ (admissible, as (1+η)ρ < 2ρ) gives limsup_i (ω_nρ^n)^{−1}μ_{T_i}(B̄_ρ(y_i)) ≤ (1 + 3c(1+η)ρ)^n(1+2η)^n μ_T(B_{(1+2η)ρ}(y))/(ω_n((1+2η)ρ)^n) + c₁(1+η)^{n+1}ρ/ω_n ≤ 1 + δ₀/2 (c₁(1+η)^{n+1} ≤ 2^{n+1}c₁). Hence (ω_nρ^n)^{−1}μ_{T_i}(B̄_ρ(y_i)) ≤ 1 + δ₀ for all sufficiently large i. With p = 2n the mean curvature term satisfies ρ^{1−n/p}(∫_{B̄_ρ(y_i)}|H|^p dμ_{T_i})^{1/p} ≤ κρ^{1−n/p}((1 + δ₀)ω_nρ^n)^{1/p} ≤ κρ(2ω_n)^{1/p} ≤ δ₀; θ ≥ 1 a.e., y_i ∈ spt V_i and B̄_ρ(y_i) ⊂ U, so the hypotheses 5.1 of Ch. 5 (where B_ρ denotes the closed ball, Ch. 1 §3) hold with centre y_i and radius ρ for all large i.
5. Allard (Ch. 5, 5.2, centre y_i, radius ρ, p = 2n): there are γ = γ(n, k, 2n) ∈ (0, 1), a linear isometry q_i of ℝ^{n+k} and a C^{1,1/2} function u_i : B^n_{γρ}(0) → ℝ^k with Du_i(0) = 0, sup|Du_i| ≤ C(n,k,2n)δ₀^{1/(2n+2)} ≤ 1/4 and spt μ_{T_i} ∩ B_{γρ}(y_i) = (y_i + q_i(graph u_i)) ∩ B_{γρ}(y_i); u_i(0) = 0 because y_i ∈ spt μ_{T_i}. Put Φ_i(v) := y_i + q_i(v, u_i(v)), σ := γρ/4, D := B^n_σ(0) and the open cylinder C_i := y_i + q_i(D × B^k_σ(0)) ⊆ B_{γρ}(y_i). As |u_i(v)| ≤ |v|/4 < σ on D, spt T_i ∩ C_i = Φ_i(D) =: M_i, and M_i is a connected embedded C¹ n-submanifold (chart Φ_i|D: injective, C¹, injective differential, Φ_i(D) = C_i ∩ M_i, proper onto M_i because M_i is relatively closed in C_i) containing y_i, with H^n(M_i) < ∞ and the continuous unit orientation ξ_i := (∧_nDΦ_i)(e_1∧⋯∧e_n)/|(∧_nDΦ_i)(e_1∧⋯∧e_n)| (transported to M_i). Constancy: let P_i(z) := first n coordinates of q_i^{−1}(z − y_i), so P_i(C_i) = D and P_i|M_i is a homeomorphism onto D (hence proper on spt(T_i⌞C_i)). Then R_i := P_{i#}(T_i⌞C_i) ∈ 𝒟_n(D) is integer multiplicity (Ch. 6, 2.24(2), 3.9) with ∂R_i = P_{i#}((∂T_i)⌞C_i) = 0, so the Constancy Theorem (Ch. 6, 2.34; D is a connected open subset of ℝ^n) gives R_i = c_i[[D]] with c_i ∈ ℤ (R_i is integer multiplicity). Since Φ_i∘P_i is C¹ and equals the identity on M_i ⊇ spt(T_i⌞C_i), the push-forward formula (Ch. 6, 2.24(2), 3.3–3.9) gives T_i⌞C_i = (Φ_i∘P_i)_#(T_i⌞C_i) = Φ_{i#}R_i = c_i[[M_i]] (M_i oriented by ξ_i). As y_i ∈ spt T_i, c_i ≠ 0. Choose ρ' > 0 with B_{ρ'}(y_i) ⊆ C_i (so B_{ρ'}(y_i) ⊆ U); then T_i(ω) = c_i∫_{M_i}⟨ω, ξ_i⟩dH^n for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with spt ω ⊆ B_{ρ'}(y_i), with c_i ∈ ℤ ∖ {0}, y_i ∈ M_i, M_i an embedded C¹ n-submanifold with continuous orientation ξ_i and H^n(M_i ∩ K) < ∞ for compact K. Hence y_i ∈ reg T_i for all large i. (Moreover |c_i| = Θ(μ_{T_i}, y_i) ≤ e^{κρ}(ω_nρ^n)^{−1}μ_{T_i}(B_ρ(y_i)) ≤ e^{κρ}(1 + δ₀) < 2, so c_i = ±1; only c_i ≠ 0 is needed.)
6. For y: Θ(μ_T, y) = 1 > 0 gives y ∈ spt T; apply steps 4–5 to the constant sequence T_i = T, y_i = y (all hypotheses hold), or directly to T, to get y ∈ reg T.
proof_key_steps: Uniform mean-curvature bound and monotonicity for T_i and T.
The retraction comparison (competitor T_i + π_#∂R̃_i) bounds limsup μ_{T_i}(B̄_ρ(y)) by μ_T near y plus O(ρ^{n+1}).
At a fixed small scale the density ratios at y_i are eventually ≤ 1 + δ₀ (the limsup bound is ≤ 1 + δ₀/2), so Allard's theorem applies.
Allard gives a C¹ graph; constancy via projection to the base plane gives T_i = c_i[[M_i]] with c_i ∈ ℤ∖{0}, so y_i ∈ reg T_i; likewise y ∈ reg T.

audit.reason: The fixed-N and uniform mass hypotheses are correctly included and used. Lemma M provides the needed upper mass estimate; the strict limsup margin gives eventual Allard hypotheses on closed balls. Projection to the base plane and constancy establish the precise oriented-current regularity conclusion.

subproblem.title: Theorem 7.4.5: a minimizing cone in a closed half-space lies in the boundary hyperplane
subproblem.statement: Let C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^{n+k}) be minimizing in ℝ^{n+k}, ∂C = 0, and a cone (η_{0,λ#}C = C for all λ > 0). If v ≠ 0 and spt C ⊆ closure{x : ⟨v,x⟩ > 0}, then spt C ⊆ frontier{x : ⟨v,x⟩ > 0} = {x : ⟨v,x⟩ = 0}.
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon 7.4.5 and its proof (chapter-07.txt lines 689–737), using the weighted first-variation identity of Ch. 4, 5.1 (chapter-04.txt lines 596–612) with H = 0 and the monotonicity identity Ch. 4, 3.6. Corrections, made explicit: the identity (1) is d/dρ[ρ^{−n}∫hφ(r/ρ)dμ] = +ρ^{−n−1}∫(x·∇^V h)φ(r/ρ)dμ (it is derived in step 4); the printed primitive ψ(x) = ∫_{|x|}^∞ rφ(r/ρ)dr has the opposite sign of the one used below, which does not affect the vanishing; φ is taken constant near 0 so that the test fields are C¹.
1. Case n = 0: a 0-current C minimizing in ℝ^k is 0 (deleting one point of a representation gives an integer multiplicity competitor of smaller mass), so spt C = ∅ and the claim holds. Assume n ≥ 1, P := n + k. Fix a representation R = (M, θ, ξ) of C (C is integer multiplicity, being minimizing) and put μ := R.measure = θH^n⌞M, the mass measure of C (Ch. 6, 3.2(3)). Then spt C = spt μ: if μ(B) = 0 for an open ball B, |C(ω)| ≤ ∫|ω|dμ = 0 for forms supported in B; if C vanishes on all forms supported in B, M_B(C) = μ(B) = 0. Let e := v/|v| and h(x) := e·x; then H := {x : 0 < ⟨v, x⟩} = {h > 0}, closure H = {h ≥ 0} and frontier H = {h = 0} (v ≠ 0).
2. Stationarity (book line 697). Apply the sibling minimizing_implies_stationary with ℓ = k, U = N = ℝ^P: univ is an embedded C² (n+k)-submanifold (chart the identity), closure univ ∖ univ = ∅, spt C ⊆ univ, C is minimizing in univ ∩ univ = univ, ∂C = 0. Hence ∫ div_M X dμ = 0 for every X ∈ C¹_c(ℝ^P; ℝ^P) (every vector is tangent to ℝ^P), where div_M X(x) = trace(p_{T_xM}∘DX(x)), T_xM the approximate tangent plane (an n-plane for μ-a.e. x).
3. Radial tangency (book line 698: "(Dr)^⊥ = 0 by virtue of the fact that C is a cone"). IsConeCurrent C gives η_{0,λ#}C = C for λ > 0; the mass measure of η_{0,λ#}C is λ^{−n}(η_{0,λ})_#μ (area formula for the homothety), so μ(λA) = λ^nμ(A) for Borel A, μ({0}) = 0, and ρ^{−n}μ(B_ρ(0)) is constant in ρ > 0. The monotonicity identity (Ch. 4, 3.6, H = 0) ρ^{−n}μ(B_ρ(0)) − σ^{−n}μ(B_σ(0)) = ∫_{B_ρ(0)∖B_σ(0)}|D^⊥r|²r^{−n}dμ (r = |x|, D^⊥r the projection of Dr = x/r onto (T_xM)^⊥) therefore gives D^⊥r = 0 μ-a.e., i.e. x^T := p_{T_xM}(x) = x for μ-a.e. x.
4. The weighted identity (book (1); Ch. 4, 5.1 with H = 0). Let φ ∈ C¹(ℝ), φ ≥ 0, constant on (−∞, δ₀] for some δ₀ > 0 and φ = 0 on [1, ∞). For ρ > 0 put I(ρ) := ∫ φ(r/ρ)h dμ. The field X_ρ(x) := φ(|x|/ρ)h(x)x is C¹ (x ↦ φ(|x|/ρ) is C¹ because φ is constant near 0) with support in B̄_ρ(0). Using div_M x = n, ∇^M(φ(r/ρ)) = ρ^{−1}φ'(r/ρ)∇^M r and x·∇^M r = |x^T|²/r = r|∇^M r|² = r(1 − |D^⊥r|²): div_M X_ρ = nφ(r/ρ)h + (r/ρ)φ'(r/ρ)(1 − |D^⊥r|²)h + φ(r/ρ)x·∇^M h. Differentiation under the integral sign (|∂_ρφ(r/ρ)| = rρ^{−2}|φ'(r/ρ)| is bounded on B_b(0) uniformly for ρ ∈ [a, b] ⊂ (0,∞), and μ(B_b(0)) < ∞) gives ρI'(ρ) = −∫(r/ρ)φ'(r/ρ)h dμ, and likewise for J(ρ) := ∫φ(r/ρ)|D^⊥r|²h dμ. Stationarity ∫div_M X_ρ dμ = 0 thus reads nI − ρI' + ρJ' + ∫φ(r/ρ)x·∇^M h dμ = 0, i.e. d/dρ[ρ^{−n}I(ρ)] = ρ^{−n}J'(ρ) + ρ^{−n−1}∫(x·∇^M h)φ(r/ρ)dμ. By step 3, J ≡ 0, so (1): d/dρ[ρ^{−n}I(ρ)] = +ρ^{−n−1}∫(x·∇^M h)φ(r/ρ)dμ for all ρ > 0.
5. The right side of (1) vanishes (book lines 708–719). Since ∇^M h = p_{T_xM}(e) and r∇^M r = x^T: x·∇^M h = e·x^T = r e·∇^M r. Let Ψ_ρ(s) := −∫_s^∞ tφ(t/ρ)dt (s ≥ 0), so Ψ_ρ'(s) = sφ(s/ρ), Ψ_ρ(s) = 0 for s ≥ ρ, and put Y_ρ(x) := Ψ_ρ(|x|)e. Then DY_ρ(x)w = (φ(|x|/ρ)x·w)e, which is continuous on ℝ^P (also at 0), so Y_ρ ∈ C¹_c(ℝ^P; ℝ^P) with spt Y_ρ ⊆ B̄_ρ(0), and div_M Y_ρ = trace(p_{T_xM}∘DY_ρ) = φ(r/ρ)(e·x^T) = rφ(r/ρ)e·∇^M r = (x·∇^M h)φ(r/ρ). By step 2, ∫(x·∇^M h)φ(r/ρ)dμ = ∫div_M Y_ρ dμ = 0. Hence ρ ↦ ρ^{−n}I(ρ) is constant on (0, ∞). (Since x^T = x a.e., the same computation shows directly ∫hφ(r/ρ)dμ = ∫div_M Y_ρ dμ = 0.)
6. Vanishing (book lines 720–735). For every admissible φ, |I(ρ)| ≤ (sup φ)∫_{B_ρ(0)}|x|dμ ≤ (sup φ)ρμ(B_ρ(0)) = (sup φ)ρ^{n+1}μ(B_1(0)), so ρ^{−n}I(ρ) → 0 as ρ ↓ 0; the constant is 0 and I(ρ) = 0 for all ρ > 0. Take φ_k(s) := χ(k(1 − s)) with χ ∈ C¹ nondecreasing, χ = 0 on (−∞, 1/2], χ = 1 on [1, ∞): φ_k is admissible (φ_k = 1 on (−∞, 1 − 1/k], φ_k = 0 on [1 − 1/(2k), ∞)) and φ_k(s) ↑ 1_{s<1}; dominated convergence (|h|1_{B_ρ(0)} ∈ L¹(μ)) gives ∫_{B_ρ(0)} h dμ = 0 for every ρ > 0.
7. Conclusion (book line 737). spt C ⊆ closure H = {h ≥ 0} and μ(ℝ^P ∖ spt μ) = 0, so h ≥ 0 μ-a.e.; with step 6, h = 0 μ-a.e. on every B_ρ(0), so μ({h > 0}) = 0. The open set {h > 0} therefore does not meet spt μ = spt C, and spt C ⊆ {h ≥ 0} ∩ {h ≤ 0} = {h = 0} = frontier H, i.e. C.support ⊆ frontier {x | 0 < ⟪v, x⟫}.
proof_key_steps: Stationarity (sibling, U = N = ℝ^P); the cone property gives D^⊥r = 0 a.e.
First variation of φ(r/ρ)h(x)x gives d/dρ[ρ^{−n}∫hφ(r/ρ)dμ] = +ρ^{−n−1}∫(x·∇^M h)φ(r/ρ)dμ.
The right side is ∫div_M(Ψ_ρ(r)e)dμ = 0 with Ψ_ρ'(s) = sφ(s/ρ); the ratio is constant, hence 0.
∫_{B_ρ}h dμ = 0 and h ≥ 0 on spt C give spt C ⊆ {h = 0} = frontier H.

audit.reason: Exact contract match. Cone scaling and stationarity imply radial tangency. The explicitly computed compactly supported test field makes the weighted integral vanish, and nonnegativity of the half-space coordinate forces support in the boundary hyperplane.

subproblem.title: Simon 7.3.3, 7.4.4, 7.5.8: integer densities and tangent planes; small singular set where Θ < 2; codimension-one regularity
subproblem.statement:
The conjunction IntegerDensityAndTangentPlanes ∧ SingularSetSmallWhereDensityBelowTwo ∧ CodimensionOneRegularity of the frozen contract (Simon 7.3.3, 7.4.4, 7.5.8), i.e. all three of the following statements, each universally quantified over all of its data.
Conventions (exactly those of the contract): ℝ^{n+k} = Euclid (n + k). "N is an embedded C² d-dimensional submanifold" means IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 2 d N: every y ∈ N has an open W ∋ y and an injective C² map ψ from an open V ⊆ ℝ^d with ψ(V) = W ∩ N, V ∩ ψ^{−1}(K) compact for every compact K ⊆ W, and Dψ injective on V. "T is minimizing in A" means IsMinimizingIn T A (Simon 7.1.1): T is integer multiplicity and M_W(T) ≤ M_W(S) for every open W with closure(W) compact and contained in U and every integer multiplicity S ∈ 𝒟_n(U) with ∂S = ∂T in U (no condition when n = 0) and spt(S − T) a compact subset of A ∩ W. "∂T = 0 in U" is BoundaryVanishes T (vacuous when n = 0). "Θ^n(μ_T, x) = θ" is HasMassDensity T x θ: θ ≥ 0 and M_{B_ρ(x)}(T)/(ω_nρ^n) → θ as ρ ↓ 0. μH[s] is the (unnormalized) s-dimensional Hausdorff measure of Mathlib, for real s. Departures, each made explicit where used: [D1] Appendix A is applied to scalar density functions, with singular-set maps defined on functions (thresholds sing^c φ := closure{⟨φ, e⟩ ≥ c}; for 3.3(2) a flatness map whose domain is recovered from the total mass and barycenter of φ), so that A.3(2) holds exactly. [D6] Remark 2.5(2) (T2), Lemma 3.5 in the special case used (T7: 1 ≤ m < n as in the book, S additionally a cone with L ⊆ T_xS μ_S-a.e., as supplied by T6) and the form of 1-dimensional minimizing cones (T8) are proved; the classification of 2-dimensional minimizing cones [Whi82] is used as cited by the book (lines 501–504).
Notation. P := n + k. For an integer multiplicity current S, μ_S is its mass measure (= R.measure for every representation R, Ch. 6, 3.2(3)), θ_S its multiplicity, Θ_S := Θ^n(μ_S, ·), spt S = spt μ_S, and M_W(S) = μ_S(W) for open W. H^n = μHE[n] = c_nμH[n] with c_n ∈ (0, ∞) (Mathlib euclideanHausdorffMeasure); ω_n = unitBallVolume n; η_{y,λ}(w) := λ^{−1}(w − y); τ_v(w) := w + v. A current is "as in T1" if it is an integer multiplicity S ∈ 𝒟_n(V), V ⊆ ℝ^P open, minimizing in V ∩ N', spt S ⊆ N', ∂S = 0 in V, where N' is an embedded C² (n+ℓ')-submanifold with (closure N' ∖ N') ∩ V = ∅.
0. (n = 0.) A 0-current S that is minimizing in V ∩ N' with spt S ⊆ N' vanishes: if a representation (M, θ, ξ) of S had a point x₀ ∈ M (H^0 is counting measure, so M is locally finite, the a.e. conditions of the representation hold at x₀, and x₀ ∈ spt S ⊆ N'), deleting x₀ gives an integer multiplicity competitor (SameBoundary is vacuous for n = 0; the support of the difference is {x₀} ⊆ N' ∩ V ∩ W for a small open ball W ⊂⊂ V) whose mass in W is smaller by θ(x₀) ≥ 1. Hence, for n = 0: in (1), T = 0 and E = F = ∅ work (Θ^0(μ_T, x) = 0 ∈ ℤ, spt T = ∅); (2) is vacuous (spt T = ∅); in (3), spt T ⊆ closure(E) ∩ U ⊆ N (as in C0 below; this inclusion does not use n ≥ 1), so T = 0 and sing T = ∅. Assume n ≥ 1 from now on.
T1 (densities). For S as in T1: by the sibling minimizing_implies_stationary and Ch. 4, 2.7 the varifold of S has generalized mean curvature with |H| ≤ √n·sup_{N'∩K}|B_{N'}| on compact K ⊆ V; monotonicity (Ch. 4, 3.17): if |H| ≤ Λ on B_R(z) ⊆ V, ρ ↦ e^{Λρ}ρ^{−n}μ_S(B_ρ(z)) is nondecreasing on (0,R). Hence Θ_S exists in [0,∞) on V, is upper semicontinuous (Ch. 4, 4.9), Θ_S = θ μ_S-a.e. (Ch. 3, Remark 1.8(2) with Theorem 1.9, as used at chapter-04.txt line 350), so Θ_S ∈ ℤ_{≥1} a.e., and Θ_S ≥ 1 on spt S ∩ V. Under η_{y,λ}: μ_{η_{y,λ#}S} = λ^{−n}(η_{y,λ})_#μ_S, Θ_{η_{y,λ#}S}(w) = Θ_S(y + λw), H scales by λ, and minimality transfers to η_{y,λ}(V) ∩ η_{y,λ}(N').
T2 (blow-up compactness with moving centres; Remark 2.5(2), lines 166–174, "left to the reader", supplied). Let S be as in T1 with |H| ≤ Λ on a ball around x ∈ V, x_j → x, λ_j > 0, λ_j → 0, S_j := η_{x_j,λ_j#}S. Then a subsequence converges weakly in ℝ^P (in the sense of currentEval) to an integer multiplicity cycle C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P), minimizing in ℝ^P, with μ_{S_j} → μ_C as Radon measures on ℝ^P. Proof: monotonicity (any centre) gives M_{B_R(0)}(S_j) = λ_j^{−n}μ_S(B_{λ_jR}(x_j)) ≤ cR^n for large j, and ∂S_j = 0 on B_R(0) for large j; Ch. 6, 2.15 (diagonally in R) and 3.11 give an integer multiplicity weak limit C with ∂C = 0. If dist(x_j, N')/λ_j is unbounded, then along a subsequence it tends to ∞, every ball B_R(0) eventually misses η_{x_j,λ_j}(N') ⊇ spt S_j, and C = 0 = lim μ_{S_j}. Otherwise dist(x_j, N') ≤ C₀λ_j, so x ∈ closure(N') ∩ V ⊆ N'. Let π be the nearest point projection onto N': it is C¹ on a ball B_δ(x) ⊂ V, maps it into N', equals the identity on N' ∩ B_δ(x), and Lip(π|B_s(w)) ≤ 1 + cs for w ∈ N' ∩ B_{δ/2}(x), s < δ/2. Fix a compact K, a cut-off ψ ∈ C^∞_c(ℝ^P; [0, 1]) with ψ = 1 near K, and G > 0 with spt ψ ⊆ B_G(0) and |y| + C₀ < G/2 for y ∈ spt ψ; take R > G. For large j, π_j := η_{x_j,λ_j}∘π∘η_{x_j,λ_j}^{−1} is C¹ on η_{x_j,λ_j}(B_δ(x)) ⊇ B_R(0), maps it into η_{x_j,λ_j}(N'), is the identity on η_{x_j,λ_j}(N') ∩ B_R(0), satisfies |π_j(y) − y| = dist(y, η_{x_j,λ_j}(N')) ≤ |y| + C₀ (so π_j(spt ψ) ⊆ B_G(0)), and L_j := Lip(π_j|B_R(0)) ≤ 1 + cλ_j(R + C₀) → 1. Run the proof of 7.2.4 (book lines 176–288; sibling compactness_of_minimizing_currents, steps 3–9) with W_s := {ψ > s}: Ch. 6, 7.2 gives C − S_j = ∂R_j + S'_j with M_{W_0}(R_j) + M_{W_0}(S'_j) → 0, and slicing (Ch. 6, 4.5) at a good level α gives C⌞W_α = S_j⌞W_α + ∂R̃_j + S̃_j with M(R̃_j) + M(S̃_j) → 0, boundary error P_j on {ψ = α} with M(P_j) → 0, and μ_{S_j}({ψ = α}) = μ_C({ψ = α}) = 0. For an integer multiplicity cycle X with spt X ⊆ K put Y_j := X + ∂R̃_j (an integer multiplicity cycle with spt Y_j ⊆ spt ψ) and Z_j := S_j + π_{j#}Y_j (π_{j#} is applied only to the compactly supported Y_j; Ch. 6, 2.29, 3.9). Then ∂Z_j = 0 and spt(Z_j − S_j) ⊆ π_j(spt Y_j), a compact subset of η_{x_j,λ_j}(N') ∩ B_G(0), so Z_j is a competitor for S_j, which is minimizing in η_{x_j,λ_j}(V) ∩ η_{x_j,λ_j}(N') (T1). Since π_j is C¹ and equals the identity on spt S_j ∩ B_R(0), its tangential differential is the identity on the approximate tangent planes μ_{S_j}-a.e., so the push-forward formula for integer multiplicity currents (Ch. 6, 2.24(2), 3.3–3.9) gives π_{j#}(S_j⌞B_G(0)) = S_j⌞B_G(0); hence Z_j⌞B_G(0) = π_{j#}((S_j + Y_j)⌞B_G(0)) and μ_{S_j}(B_G(0)) ≤ μ_{Z_j}(B_G(0)) ≤ L_j^nμ_{S_j+Y_j}(B_G(0)). As S_j + Y_j = S_j off {ψ ≥ α}, comparing as in 2.4 (book (9)–(11)) gives M_{W_α}(S_j) ≤ M_{W_α}(C + X) + ε_j with ε_j := M(S̃_j) + M(P_j) + (L_j^n − 1)Λ_G → 0, where Λ_G := sup_j μ_{S_j+Y_j}(B_G(0)) ≤ cG^n + M(X) + sup_j M(∂R̃_j) < ∞ (∂R̃_j = (C − S_j)⌞W_α − S̃_j). Lower semicontinuity of mass (SimonGMT WeaklyConvergesOn.massOn_le_liminf) gives M_{W_α}(C) ≤ M_{W_α}(C + X); hence C is minimizing in ℝ^P (localize to an arbitrary open W ⊂⊂ ℝ^P as in step 8 of the compactness sibling), and with X = 0, limsup_j μ_{S_j}(K) ≤ μ_C(K); with lower semicontinuity on open sets and the layer-cake formula, μ_{S_j} → μ_C (for a subsequence of every subsequence, hence for the subsequence).
T3 (semicontinuity along sequences). Let S_i ∈ 𝒟_n(V_i), S ∈ 𝒟_n(V) be as in T1 with |H| ≤ Λ, every compact subset of V contained in V_i for large i, and μ_{S_i} → μ_S on V. If y_i → y ∈ V then Θ_S(y) ≥ limsup Θ_{S_i}(y_i), and if y_i ∈ spt S_i infinitely often then y ∈ spt S. Proof: for B̄_{3ρ}(y) ⊆ V, δ < ρ and large i, monotonicity gives Θ_{S_i}(y_i) ≤ e^{Λρ}μ_{S_i}(B̄_{ρ+δ}(y))/(ω_nρ^n), and limsup_i μ_{S_i}(B̄_{ρ+δ}(y)) ≤ μ_S(B̄_{ρ+δ}(y)); let δ ↓ 0, ρ ↓ 0. If y_i ∈ spt S_i, μ_{S_i}(B̄_{ρ+δ}(y)) ≥ e^{−Λρ}ω_nρ^n, so μ_S(B̄_{ρ+δ}(y)) > 0.
T4 (the class 𝒯; book 3.3(1)(6)–(10)). Fix z, r with B̄_{2r}(z) ⊂ U; T' := (η_{z,r#}T)⌞B_2(0) is as in T1 (V = B_2(0), N' = η_{z,r}(N); competitors extend by T), m₀ := μ_{T'}(B_2(0)) < ∞, |H_{T'}| ≤ Λ₀ on B_2(0); assume T' ≠ 0 and let b₀ be the barycenter of μ_{T'}. 𝒯 consists of pairs (S, U_S): x_i → x, λ_i → λ ∈ [0,1], λ_i ∈ (0,1), |x_i| < 1 − λ_i, U_S := η_{x,λ}(B_2(0)) = B_{2/λ}(−x/λ) if λ > 0, U_S := ℝ^P if λ = 0, and η_{x_i,λ_i#}T' → S on 𝒟^n(U_S); (x, λ) are the parameters. (a) If λ > 0, S = η_{x,λ#}T', U_S ⊇ B_2(0) (|x| ≤ 1 − λ), μ_S(ℝ^P) = λ^{−n}m₀ ∈ (0,∞), spt μ_S ⊆ B̄_{2/λ}(−x/λ), barycenter (b₀ − x)/λ, |H_S| ≤ Λ₀; (T', B_2(0)) ∈ 𝒯. (b) If λ = 0, the defining blow-ups are blow-ups of T at z + rx_i → z + rx, so by T2 S is an integer multiplicity cycle minimizing in ℝ^P with H = 0 and μ-convergence on ℝ^P; monotonicity gives μ_S(B_ρ(w)) ≥ ω_nρ^n for w ∈ spt S, so μ_S(ℝ^P) ∈ {0,∞}. (c) (η_{y,λ'#}S, η_{y,λ'}(U_S)) ∈ 𝒯 for 0 < λ' < 1, |y| ≤ 1 − λ', with parameters (x + λy, λλ') (η_{y,λ'}∘η_{x_i,λ_i} = η_{x_i+λ_iy,λ_iλ'}, |x_i + λ_iy| < 1 − λ_iλ'). (d) Every sequence in 𝒯 has a subsequence converging weakly on compact subsets of the limit domain to a member S, with μ-convergence on ℝ^P: if the parameters converge to (x*, λ*) with λ* > 0 use (a) and dominated convergence; if λ* = 0, replace each member by a blow-up D_k of T' with nearby parameters (λ'_k → 0) that is 1/k-close in metrics for weak and vague convergence (metrizable on the family, which has uniform bounds μ(B_R(0)) ≤ max(c, m₀)R^n), and apply T2. (e) For a member S, |y| < 1 and λ_k ↓ 0, a subsequence of η_{y,λ_k#}S converges, with μ-convergence on ℝ^P, to a member C with parameters (·, 0) which is a cone: for λ > 0 apply the sibling density_and_tangent_cones (2) to T at z + r(x + λy) (or C = 0 if x + λy ∉ spt T'); for λ = 0 apply it to S (U = N = ℝ^P, ℓ = k) at y and diagonalize as in (d). (f) A member with μ_S(λA) = λ^nμ_S(A) (λ > 0), or with μ_S(ℝ^P) = ∞, has parameter λ = 0.
T5 (functions; Q = 1, e the unit vector of Euclid 1). φ_S(w) := ϑ_S(w)e, ϑ_S(w) := limsup_{ρ↓0}μ_S(B_ρ(w))/(ω_nρ^n) if finite, else 0 (μ_S extended by 0 off U_S). (i) ϑ_S = Θ_S on U_S. (ii) ϑ_S is Borel. (iii) μ_S = ϑ_SμHE[n] (Θ^n(μ_S,·) = θ a.e. on the carrier and 0 a.e. off it, Ch. 1 §3). (iv) Hence φ_S is locally μH[n]-integrable and (H0) holds: a.e. equal functions give equal μ_S, hence equal φ_S everywhere. (v) φ_{S_i} ⇀ φ_S weakly iff μ_{S_i} → μ_S on ℝ^P. (vi) φ_{η_{y,λ#}S}(w) = φ_S(y + λw). (vii) φ_C(λw) = φ_C(w) for cones C. With F := {φ_S : (S, U_S) ∈ 𝒯}: (H0), integrability, A.1 (T4(c), (vi)), A.2 (T4(e), (v), (vii)) hold. If φ_S is homogeneous, or φ_S = c·1_L with ⟨c, e⟩ ≠ 0 (L an n-plane), then S has parameter 0 (T4(f), (iii)); for parameter-0 members {Θ_S ≥ c'} is closed in ℝ^P (T1).
T6 (invariance). If S has parameter 0 and φ_S(y + λw) = φ_S(w) (y ∈ L, λ > 0), then μ_S is L-translation invariant and ρ^{−n}μ_S(B_ρ(z)) is constant for z ∈ L; S is stationary (sibling minimizing_implies_stationary), so the monotonicity identity (Ch. 4, 3.6) gives x − z ∈ T_xS a.e. for a countable dense set of z ∈ L, hence x ∈ T_xS and L ⊆ T_xS a.e.; then x ∧ S⃗ = 0 = v ∧ S⃗ (v ∈ L) a.e., and the homotopy formula (Ch. 6, 2.25–2.27, 2.33; ∂S = 0) gives η_{0,λ#}S = S and τ_{v#}S = S.
T7 (Lemma 3.5 for invariant cones; book lines 410–418, proof "left to the reader", supplied; with the book's restriction 1 ≤ m < n, and for cones with L ⊆ T_xS a.e., which is the case used below). Let 1 ≤ m < n, write ℝ^P = ℝ^m × ℝ^{P−m} with p(t, y) := t, q(t, y) := y, L := ℝ^m × {0}, and let S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) be integer multiplicity and minimizing in ℝ^P with ∂S = 0, η_{0,λ#}S = S for all λ > 0, τ_{v#}S = S for all v ∈ L, and L ⊆ T_xS for μ_S-a.e. x. Then there is an integer multiplicity S₀ ∈ 𝒟_{n−m}(ℝ^{P−m}), of dimension n − m ≥ 1, with S = [[ℝ^m]] × S₀ (product of Ch. 6, 2.17–2.22), μ_S = L^m ⊗ μ_{S₀}, ∂S₀ = 0, η_{0,λ#}S₀ = S₀ for all λ > 0, and S₀ minimizing in ℝ^{P−m} (7.1.1 with competitors S₀' satisfying ∂S₀' = ∂S₀, a genuine condition because n − m ≥ 1). For an m-dimensional subspace L other than ℝ^m × {0} the same holds after a rotation, which preserves all hypotheses and conclusions. Proof. (a) Product structure. Let S = τ(M, θ, ξ). For μ_S-a.e. x, T_xS = L ⊕ (T_xS ∩ L^⊥), so after fixing signs ξ(x) = e_1 ∧ ⋯ ∧ e_m ∧ ζ(x) with ζ(x) a unit simple (n−m)-vector orienting T_xS ∩ L^⊥, and the coarea factor of p|M is 1 (p restricted to T_xS is the orthogonal projection onto L ⊆ T_xS). For ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P) let ω♭ := Σ_{J ⊆ {m+1,…,P}, |J| = n−m} ω_{(1,…,m)J}dx^J (the coefficient of dt^1∧⋯∧dt^m); then ⟨ω, ξ⟩ = ⟨ω♭, ζ⟩ μ_S-a.e. Slicing successively by t^1, …, t^m (Ch. 6, 4.1–4.5; [Fed69, 4.3.1–4.3.8]) and the coarea formula on the countably n-rectifiable M give, for L^m-a.e. t, integer multiplicity (n−m)-currents ⟨S, p, t⟩ = τ(M ∩ p^{−1}(t), θ, ζ) with ∂⟨S, p, t⟩ = ±⟨∂S, p, t⟩ = 0, and S(ω) = ∫_{ℝ^m}⟨S, p, t⟩(ω♭)dt for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P). Since τ_{v#}S = S and p∘τ_v = p + v, ⟨S, p, t + v⟩ = τ_{v#}⟨S, p, t⟩ for L^{2m}-a.e. (t, v) ∈ ℝ^m × ℝ^m (v ≅ (v, 0) ∈ L); by Fubini there is t₀ with ⟨S, p, t⟩ = τ_{(t − t₀)#}⟨S, p, t₀⟩ for a.e. t. Put S₀ := q_#⟨S, p, t₀⟩, an integer multiplicity (n−m)-cycle in ℝ^{P−m}; then ⟨S, p, t⟩ = [[t]] × S₀ for a.e. t, so S(ω) = ∫_{ℝ^m}S₀(ω♭(t, ·))dt = ([[ℝ^m]] × S₀)(ω), and μ_S = L^m ⊗ μ_{S₀} (coarea factor 1). (b) Cone. η_{0,λ}(t, y) = (t/λ, y/λ) and η_{0,λ#}[[ℝ^m]] = [[ℝ^m]], so [[ℝ^m]] × η_{0,λ#}S₀ = η_{0,λ#}S = S = [[ℝ^m]] × S₀; testing with ω = φ(t)dt^1∧⋯∧dt^m∧β(y), ∫φ = 1, recovers the factor, so η_{0,λ#}S₀ = S₀. (c) Minimality (this is where n − m ≥ 1 is used). Let W₀ ⊂⊂ ℝ^{P−m} be open and S₀' integer multiplicity with ∂S₀' = ∂S₀ = 0 and spt(S₀' − S₀) a compact subset of W₀, and suppose M_{W₀}(S₀') = M_{W₀}(S₀) − δ with δ > 0. X₀ := S₀' − S₀ is an integer multiplicity cycle (Ch. 6, 3.2(1)) of dimension n − m ≥ 1 with compact support in W₀. Because n − m ≥ 1, the cone Y₀ := 0 ⨯ X₀ = h_#([[(0, 1)]] × X₀), h(s, y) := sy (Ch. 6, 2.30), is an integer multiplicity (n−m+1)-current with compact support and ∂Y₀ = X₀ − 0 ⨯ ∂X₀ = X₀ (Ch. 6, 2.31; for a 0-dimensional X₀ the boundary would contain the additional term −X₀(1)[[0]], which is why m = n is excluded). subproblem.title: Theorem 7.4.2: the regular set is dense in the support
subproblem.statement: Let ℓ ≤ k, U ⊆ ℝ^{n+k} open, N an embedded C² (n+ℓ)-submanifold with (N̄∖N) ∩ U = ∅, and T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) minimizing in U ∩ N with spt T ⊆ U ∩ N and ∂T = 0 in U. Then spt T ⊆ closure(reg T).
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon 7.4.2 (chapter-07.txt lines 605–612: "an immediate consequence of the Allard Theorem 5.2 of Ch. 5 and Lemma 1.2"). The omitted argument is Simon Ch. 5, Corollary 7.3 and its proof (chapter-05.txt lines 1378–1395), in which the use of Allard's theorem (Ch. 5, 7.1) is supplied here by the sibling density_one_implies_regular.
1. If n = 0 then T = 0 (a minimizing 0-current supported in N loses mass when a point is deleted), so spt T = ∅. Assume n ≥ 1. Fix a representation T = τ(M, θ, ξ); μ_T = θH^n⌞M.
2. Density facts. By the sibling density_and_tangent_cones (part (1); spt ∂T = ∅), Θ(x) := Θ^n(μ_T, x) exists for every x ∈ U and is upper semicontinuous on U. Moreover Θ = θ μ_T-a.e. (Ch. 3, Remark 1.8(2) with Theorem 1.9, as used in Ch. 4 at chapter-04.txt line 350: densities of θH^n⌞M), so Θ is a positive integer μ_T-a.e. If x ∈ spt T, every ball B_r(x) has μ_T(B_r(x)) > 0, hence contains points w_j → x with Θ(w_j) ∈ ℤ_{≥1}; by upper semicontinuity Θ(x) ≥ 1.
3. Choice of a point (Ch. 5, proof of 7.3). Let x ∈ spt T and ρ > 0 with B_ρ(x) ⊆ U; we show reg T ∩ B_ρ(x) ≠ ∅. Let N₀ := min{j ∈ ℤ_{≥1} : Θ(z) = j for some z ∈ B_ρ(x)} (the set is nonempty by step 2). At μ_T-a.e. point of B_ρ(x), Θ is an integer ≥ N₀; as in step 2, upper semicontinuity gives Θ ≥ N₀ at every point of spt T ∩ B_ρ(x), hence θ ≥ N₀ μ_T-a.e. in B_ρ(x). Pick z₀ ∈ B_ρ(x) with Θ(z₀) = N₀ (so z₀ ∈ spt T ⊆ N) and, by upper semicontinuity, r > 0 with B_r(z₀) ⊆ B_ρ(x) and Θ < N₀ + 1 on B_r(z₀). Then θ = N₀ μ_T-a.e. in B_r(z₀).
4. The reduced current. Let U₀ := B_r(z₀) and T₀ := N₀^{−1}·(T restricted to U₀) ∈ 𝒟_n(U₀). T₀ = τ(M ∩ U₀, 1, ξ) up to a μ_T-null set, so it is integer multiplicity; ∂T₀ = 0 in U₀; spt T₀ ⊆ N; (N̄∖N) ∩ U₀ = ∅; and T₀ is minimizing in U₀ ∩ N: if W ⊂⊂ U₀ is open and S₀ is an integer multiplicity competitor for T₀ (∂S₀ = 0, spt(S₀ − T₀) ⊆ U₀ ∩ N ∩ W compact), then S := T + N₀(S₀ − T₀) (the compactly supported difference extended by zero) is an integer multiplicity competitor for T, with M_W(S) = N₀M_W(S₀) and M_W(T) = N₀M_W(T₀) (multiplicity N₀ a.e. on W ∩ M; the competitor S₀ − T₀ changes T only inside W), so M_W(T₀) ≤ M_W(S₀). Also sup M_W(T₀) < ∞ for W ⊂⊂ U₀, and Θ^n(μ_{T₀}, z₀) = Θ(z₀)/N₀ = 1.
5. Apply the sibling density_one_implies_regular with U := U₀, the constant sequences T_i := T₀, y_i := z₀, limit T₀ and y := z₀ (z₀ ∈ N ∩ U₀, z₀ ∈ spt T₀, HasMassDensity T₀ z₀ 1). It gives z₀ ∈ reg T₀: there are ρ' > 0 with B_{ρ'}(z₀) ⊆ U₀, m ∈ ℤ∖{0}, and an embedded oriented C¹ submanifold M' ∋ z₀ of locally finite H^n-measure with T₀ = m[[M']] in B_{ρ'}(z₀). Then T = N₀m[[M']] in B_{ρ'}(z₀) ⊆ U, with N₀m ≠ 0 and z₀ ∈ spt T, so z₀ ∈ reg T ∩ B_ρ(x).
6. Since ρ was arbitrary, x ∈ closure(reg T); hence spt T ⊆ closure(reg T).

Near a point of least integer density N₀ in a ball, T/N₀ is a minimizing cycle with density 1.
density_one_implies_regular (constant sequences) gives a regular point in every ball.

subproblem.title: Corollary 7.5.11: a component of the regular set, with multiplicity one, is a minimizing cycle
subproblem.statement: Let U ⊆ ℝ^{n+k} be open, N ∈ 𝒪 (oriented embedded C² (n+1)-submanifold, (N̄∖N) ∩ U = ∅, N ∩ U ≠ ∅) with orientation ξ_N, E ⊆ N ∩ U measurable, T = ∂[[E]] in U, T minimizing in N ∩ U. Let T = τ(M, θ, ξ) be any integer multiplicity representation, y ∈ reg T, M₁ the connected component of reg T containing y, and T₁ ∈ 𝒟_n(U) with T₁(ω) = ∫_{M₁} ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dH^n. Then ∂T₁ = 0 in U and T₁ is minimizing in U ∩ N.
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon 7.5.11 and its proof (chapter-07.txt lines 976–1016), Lemma 7.1.4 (lines 62–79), Remark 5.2(‡) (lines 757–765). Departures: [D1] the printed cut-off "ζ = Π φ_j" must be ζ = Π(1 − φ_j) (ζ has to vanish near the singular points); [D2] the printed pointwise bound "|d(ζω) − ζdω| ≤ c|ω|Σσ_j^{n−1}" is replaced by the integrated estimate of step 4, which uses the monotonicity mass bound; [D3] a second cut-off χ separates M₁ from the rest of spt T (needed because ζ only vanishes near sing T).
1. If n = 0 then T = 0 (minimizing 0-currents vanish), reg T = ∅ and the statement is vacuous. Assume n ≥ 1 (then k ≥ 1, as N has dimension n+1). spt T ⊆ closure(E) ∩ U ⊆ N, and ∂T = 0 (T(dω) = ∫_E⟨ddω, ξ_N⟩ = 0).
2. Structure. By 5.2(‡) (Ch. 6, 2.35 in charts of N and De Giorgi's structure theorem, Ch. 3, 4.3), θ = 1 μ_T-a.e. reg T is relatively open in spt T, and every z ∈ reg T has a ball B_r(z) with spt T ∩ B_r(z) = M' ∩ B_r(z) a connected C¹ graph (shrinking the ball of the definition; M' is relatively closed in a neighbourhood of z by properness of the chart). Hence reg T is a locally connected C¹ n-manifold, M₁ is relatively open in spt T, and: (a) closure(M₁) ∖ M₁ ⊆ sing T, and (b) closure(spt T ∖ M₁) ∩ M₁ = ∅ (near z ∈ M₁ all of spt T lies on the connected sheet through z, which lies in M₁). On M₁, H^n(M₁ ∖ M) = 0 and ξ orients T_xM₁ a.e., θ = 1 a.e. Thus T₁ = T⌞M₁ = τ(M₁, 1, ξ) is integer multiplicity, T₂ := T − T₁ = T⌞(U∖M₁) = τ(M∖M₁, θ, ξ) is integer multiplicity, and μ_T = μ_{T₁} + μ_{T₂}, so M_W(T₁) + M_W(T₂) = M_W(T) for every open W.
3. Size of the singular set. By the third conjunct (CodimensionOneRegularity) of the sibling dimension_reduction_results: sing T = ∅ if n ≤ 6; sing T ∩ K is finite for compact K ⊂ U if n = 7; μH[n−1](sing T) = 0 if n > 7 (take α = 6). In all cases H^{n−1}(sing T ∩ K) = 0 for compact K ⊂ U (for n = 1, sing T ∩ K = ∅).
4. ∂T₁ = 0 (book (1),(2)). Let ω ∈ 𝒟^{n−1}(U), K := spt ω. By the sibling minimizing_implies_stationary and monotonicity (Ch. 4, 3.17) there are C, r₁ > 0 with μ_T(B_r(ξ')) ≤ Cr^n for ξ' ∈ K, r < r₁. Z := closure(M₁) ∩ K ∖ M₁ is compact and ⊆ sing T (2(a)), so H^{n−1}(Z) = 0. Given ε ∈ (0,1), cover Z by finitely many balls B_{σ_j}(ξ_j), ξ_j ∈ Z, σ_j < r₁/2, Σ_j σ_j^{n−1} < ε (for n = 1, Z = ∅). Take φ_j ∈ C^∞_c(B_{2σ_j}(ξ_j); [0,1]), φ_j = 1 on B_{σ_j}(ξ_j), |Dφ_j| ≤ 2/σ_j, and ζ := Π_j(1 − φ_j) [D1]. K₁ := closure(M₁) ∩ spt(ζω) is a compact subset of M₁, so by 2(b) there is χ ∈ C^∞_c(U), χ = 1 near K₁, χ = 0 near closure(spt T ∖ M₁) ∩ spt(ζω) [D3]. Since spt T₁ ⊆ closure(M₁) and spt T₂ ⊆ closure(spt T ∖ M₁): T₁(d(ζω)) = T₁(d(χζω)) = T(d(χζω)) = ∂T(χζω) = 0 (book (2)). Now d(ζω) = dζ ∧ ω + ζ dω and |dζ| ≤ Σ_j |Dφ_j|, so (book lines 1010–1016, [D2]) |T₁(dω)| = |T₁(d((1−ζ)ω))| ≤ ‖ω‖_∞ Σ_j (2/σ_j) μ_T(B_{2σ_j}(ξ_j)) + ‖dω‖_∞ Σ_j μ_T(B_{2σ_j}(ξ_j)) ≤ C2^{n+1}(‖ω‖_∞ + ‖dω‖_∞) Σ_j σ_j^{n−1} ≤ C'ε. Letting ε ↓ 0, T₁(dω) = 0. Hence BoundaryVanishes T₁.
5. Minimality (Lemma 1.4, book lines 67–79, in the contract's competitor form; cf. SimonGMT Chapter07.minimizing_summands_source). Let W ⊂⊂ U be open and S an integer multiplicity current with ∂S = ∂T₁ = 0 and spt(S − T₁) a compact subset of U ∩ N ∩ W. Then S + T₂ is integer multiplicity (Ch. 6, 3.2(1)), ∂(S + T₂) = ∂T, and spt((S + T₂) − T) = spt(S − T₁), so minimality of T in N ∩ U gives M_W(T₁) + M_W(T₂) = M_W(T) ≤ M_W(S + T₂) ≤ M_W(S) + M_W(T₂). As M_W(T₂) ≤ M_W(T) < ∞, M_W(T₁) ≤ M_W(S). Together with step 2, T₁ is minimizing in U ∩ N.
proof_key_steps: θ = 1 a.e.; reg T is a C¹ manifold, M₁ is relatively open in spt T and its frontier lies in sing T.
H^{n−1}(sing T ∩ K) = 0 by the CodimensionOneRegularity conjunct of dimension_reduction_results.
Cut-offs around the singular frontier and the monotonicity bound give ∂T₁ = 0.
Mass additivity (Lemma 1.4) transfers minimality to T₁.
